drafts.title: $50,000 just to reserve it. $250,000 for the thrusters. What I want for my Model Y (AP5, EV quote-post / Tesla fan morning-after)
drafts.window: Fri ~2 PM MT (keeps 11 AM-12 PM for F1).
drafts.angle: morning-after take. He already posted "Here we go" during the stream. Now the regular-family opinion: fun show, but what reaches a $40k car. Different from the live unveil quote.
bullets: Tesla showed the new Roadster Thu Oct 15 near McGregor, Texas: drove upside down on a ramp, turned in the air and jumped over a truck using SpaceX cold-gas thrusters (TechCrunch, The Verge, Reuters via Mint).
Three trims: Performance (two seats, road ready), Thrust (two seats, rear thrusters, limited release) and Rocket (one seat, invite only, not approved for public roads, per The Verge).
Claims: over 300 miles of range, over 230 mph, 0-60 under 1 second with thrusters. Production in 2028. No full price given.
Reservations: $50,000 for Performance ($5,000 today, $45,000 within 10 days) and $250,000 for Thrust (Tesla reservation page, Reuters).
2017 promise was 620 miles, $200,000, deliveries in 2020. The event ran under 30 minutes (The Verge).
Pixel: skip, or 10 sec: "Cool car. I want the cheap version of whatever they learned."
Premium reply/quote: quote @Tesla Roadster post or Sawyer Merritt's recap. One line: "Cool. Now put [the feature] in the $40k car."
Twin check: his "Here we go" quote and the @wholemars interior reply are LIVE. This is the price-and-trickle-down opinion, a different post.
drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:
$50,000 just to hold a spot. $250,000 if you want the thrusters.

Fun show. I'll never own one. What I want is [the feature] in my Model Y.

Musk says production starts 2028. [quote: @Tesla's Roadster clip]

What would you want to trickle down?

LONGER VERSION:
Watched the Roadster show from Kentucky last night. Upside-down ramp, thrusters, a jump over a truck. Cool car.

$50,000 just to reserve the Performance. $250,000 if you want the Thrust version with the rear thrusters. Production maybe 2028. No sticker price yet.

I'm not the guy who buys that. I'm the guy who just drove a Model Y 1,500 miles to see family.

What I care about is what trickles down. Better batteries, safer software, cheaper powertrains in a $40,000 car. The original Roadster paid for the Model S, and that paid for the car in my garage.

If one thing from that show ends up in a normal family EV, that's the win. What would you want it to be?
